# Python compatibility fixtures and baseline

`python-v0.1.1.bundle`, `python-v0.1.1.sqlite3`, and `python-v0.1.1.json` were generated using the untouched Python 0.1.1 prototype before its removal. The bundle includes r0 and an attributed r1 adding `original.txt`; the SQLite file has the original leases/workspaces schema and registered actor `fixture`. No secrets or customer data are included. The manifest records the baseline and accepted head hashes. Test setup fetches these refs into a new bare repository and copies the original SQLite bytes, then tests reading and writing both `.mai` and `.agenttrunk` naming. The legacy baseline ref is changed only inside disposable tests. The absent registered fixture workspace also exercises existing registry compatibility.

The original suite passed all 17 tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` (2.583 seconds in this workspace). `python` was unavailable, so the exact older documented command could not run; `python3` ran the same tests. No original tests were removed before their behavioral requirements were inspected and ported.

Rust equivalents cover disjoint stale integration/history/provenance, overlapping rejection and draft preservation, lease block/release, component prefixes, executable/deletion, checks, dirty refresh/discard, two/eight concurrent writers, directory/file replacement, clean JSON check output, Git mirror, Git import r0, both repository naming formats, benchmark integrity, version, and JSON status. Version/JSON cases share one Rust test; new cases extend separate-process fanout, contention, same-agent duplication, binary/symlink/rename handling, expiration/path errors, Git CAS, disabled hooks, remote divergence, unsupported filenames, workspace symlink/foreign-authority rejection, and interrupted acceptance recovery including actual CLI process termination. Tests and benchmarks require only Rust, Git, and local disposable storage.

Final local validation: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-targets --locked` (32 tests), release builds of both binaries, installation into a temporary prefix, shell syntax checks, and the native demo passed. Runtime init/workspace/submit also passed with a PATH exposing Git but no Python. Cargo used a temporary cache (`CARGO_HOME=/tmp/mai-cargo`) because the normal cache was read-only. Git status/tracked-file verification was unavailable: the provided `.git` directory had no repository metadata. No commits, upstream pushes, releases, packages, or production assets were published/migrated. CI is configured for Linux/macOS but was not run remotely; macOS and the declared minimum Rust version were not tested locally. The benchmark burst failures are documented separately, not counted as passing checks.
